study type: Retrospective population-based study using national birth registry data
exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal, intrapartum cesarean, combined)
cohort: The study included all live births in Brazil registered in the national birth e-Registry (SINASC) from 2011 to 2014, encompassing both twin and singleton pregnancies.
finding: Twin pregnancies in Brazil had a prevalence of 1.13% and were associated with significantly worse perinatal outcomes, including higher rates of preterm birth, low birth weight, and low Apgar scores, particularly for the second twin, compared to singletons.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery, intrapartum cesarean, and combined delivery were associated with a 5-minute Apgar score < 7 among twins.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was an outcome assessed (specific weight range not mentioned).
gest_age: Preterm birth <32 weeks was an outcome assessed.
